\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Maiorana–McFarland sign function]
\lean{FABL.maioranaMcFarlandPermutation}
\label{FABL.maioranaMcFarlandPermutation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.Sign, FABL.binarySign, FABL.f₂CubeBlockEquiv, FABL.f₂DotProduct, FABL.signValue}
For a nonnegative integer $n$, let $\pi$ be a permutation of the binary cube of
dimension $n$, and let $g$ assign a sign in $\{-1,1\}$ to each point of that cube. The
resulting function on the binary cube of dimension $2n$ sends a point, written as a pair
$(x,y)$ of binary $n$-tuples, to $(-1)^{x\cdot\pi(y)}g(y)$, where the dot product is
computed in $\mathbb F_2$ and its value is interpreted as an integer sign.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Permutation construction on joined cube blocks]
\lean{FABL.maioranaMcFarlandPermutation_joinF₂CubeBlocks}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.Sign, FABL.binarySign, FABL.f₂DotProduct, FABL.joinF₂CubeBlocks, FABL.maioranaMcFarlandPermutation, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\pi$ be a permutation of the $n$-dimensional cube
over $\mathbb F_2$, and let $g$ map that cube to $\{\pm1\}$. For any $x,y\in\mathbb
F_2^n$, the function on the joined blocks $(x,y)$ defined by the permutation
construction has value
\[(-1)^{\langle x,\pi(y)\rangle}\,g(y),\]
where the inner product is taken in $\mathbb F_2$ and the exponent is interpreted as the
associated real sign.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficient of a permuted Maiorana–McFarland function]
\lean{FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_maioranaMcFarlandPermutation_joinF₂CubeBlocks}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.Sign, FABL.binarySign, FABL.expect_innerProductModTwo_mul_vectorWalshCharacter, FABL.f₂CubeBlockEquiv, FABL.f₂DotProduct, FABL.joinF₂CubeBlocks, FABL.maioranaMcFarlandPermutation, FABL.maioranaMcFarlandPermutation_joinF₂CubeBlocks, FABL.signValue, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_eq_expect, FABL.vectorWalshCharacter, FABL.vectorWalshCharacter_joinF₂CubeBlocks, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{6}
Let $\pi$ be a permutation of the $n$-dimensional binary cube, let $g$ assign a sign to
each point of that cube, and let $a,b$ be points of the cube. The vector Fourier
coefficient of the permuted Maiorana–McFarland function at the concatenation of $a$ and
$b$ is $2^{-n}$ times the real value of the sign assigned by $g$ to $\pi^{-1}(a)$,
multiplied by the Walsh character indexed by $b$ evaluated at $\pi^{-1}(a)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sign-valued permuted Maiorana–McFarland function]
\lean{FABL.isSignValued_maioranaMcFarlandPermutation}
\label{FABL.isSignValued_maioranaMcFarlandPermutation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.IsSignValued, FABL.Sign, FABL.abs_vectorWalshCharacter, FABL.binarySign, FABL.f₂CubeBlockEquiv, FABL.f₂DotProduct, FABL.joinF₂CubeBlocks, FABL.maioranaMcFarlandPermutation, FABL.maioranaMcFarlandPermutation_joinF₂CubeBlocks, FABL.signValue_eq_neg_one_or_one, FABL.vectorWalshCharacter_apply}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\pi$ be a permutation of $\mathbb F_2^n$, and let
$g:\mathbb F_2^n\to\{\pm1\}$. For each pair of blocks $(x,y)\in\mathbb
F_2^n\times\mathbb F_2^n$, the function $(-1)^{x\cdot\pi(y)}g(y)$ has absolute value
$1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bentness under a permutation]
\lean{FABL.isBent_maioranaMcFarlandPermutation}
\label{FABL.isBent_maioranaMcFarlandPermutation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.IsBent, FABL.Sign, FABL.abs_vectorWalshCharacter, FABL.f₂CubeBlockEquiv, FABL.joinF₂CubeBlocks, FABL.maioranaMcFarlandPermutation, FABL.signValue, FABL.signValue_eq_neg_one_or_one, FABL.vectorFourierCoeff_maioranaMcFarlandPermutation_joinF₂CubeBlocks}
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $n$, every permutation $[4m[0m":[n]\to\{0,1\}^n$ of the
$n$-dimensional binary cube, and every function $g$ from that cube to the signs, the
permutation-based Maiorana–McFarland function on the $2n$-dimensional binary cube is
bent: every Fourier coefficient has absolute value $2^{-n}$.
\end{theorem}
